The key distrinction of parallel computing is between **shared memory** and **distributed memory** models. The former allows multiple threads to access the same memory space, while the latter requires explicit communication between processes, and these two models are represented in the two main libraries for parallel computing: **OpenMP** and **MPI** respectively. These notes will cover a basic introduction to both of these libraries, and how they can be used to parallelize code. Both are used in high-performance computing (HPC) to speed up computations by distributing the workload across multiple processors or cores. 

Both MPI and OpenMP have mature implementations in C/C++ and Fortran, but this post will focus on the C/C++ implementations.

## MPI


* **Distributed memory model**
  → Decompose domain into regions owned by processes
  → Each sub-domain has a *halo* of cells that is passed to the neighbouring domains during communication stage.

#### Illustration (Halo Exchange):

```
        A        B        C
    ┌────┐┌────┐┌────┐
   A_L  A_R B_L  B_R C_L  C_R

Step 1: Right
A_R → B  
B_R → C  
C_R → A

Step 2: Left  
C_L → B  
B_L → A  
A_L → C
```

* Ensure each boundary has **2 buffers** — one to receive and one to send → **halo exchange**.

---

### **Basic Commands**

```c
MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);

MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);

MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);

MPI_Finalize();
```

---

### **Send/Receive**

```c
MPI_Send(&data, count, type, dest, tag, MPI_COMM_WORLD);

MPI_Recv(&data, count, type, source, tag, MPI_COMM_WORLD);
```

### **MPI (continued)**

* **Initialization and data output** can be done with **gather/scatter**

  ```c
  MPI_Scatter     P0   A B C     →    P0 A  
                                 →    P1 B  
                                 →    P2 C

  MPI_Gather      P2            →    P0  A B C
                  P1
                  P0
  ```

* `MPI_Barrier` is also important to **block all processes** so all can catch up.

* There will be **2 send/recv calls per dimension**

* **Must include headers:**

  ```c
  #include <mpi.h>
  ```

* **Non-blocking communication** can be used to avoid processes stalling while waiting for messages

  ```c
  MPI_Isend / Irecv
  ```

* The **Boost.MPI** library has modern **C++ bindings** for MPI.
  These work in a similar way, although STL types must use:
  → `Boost.Serialization`

* Also use **cartesian communicators** when doing **grid-like** domain decomposition.

A hello world program in MPI:
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <mpi.h>

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {

  
int my_rank,p;

  MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);
  
MPI_Comm_rank ( MPI_COMM_WORLD, &my_rank );
  
MPI_Comm_size ( MPI_COMM_WORLD, &p );

  
printf("Hello B2.02 from rank %d of %d\n",
	 my_rank,p);

  
MPI_Finalize();

  return(EXIT_SUCCESS);

}
```


A send recieve program


```c
//mpi test program
//compile with mpicxx mpitest.cpp -o mpitest
//run with mpiexec -n <num> ./mpitest
#include <iostream>
#include <mpi.h>

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {

  int rank, size;

  //initialise mpi communicator
  MPI_Init(&argc,&argv);
  MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);
  MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);

  //initialise an array and fill
  int arrsize=10;
  int* arr=new int[arrsize];

  for (int i = 0; i < arrsize; i++) {
    arr[i]=i*(rank+1);
  }

  //pass around in a circle to the process rank+1
  int my_right=rank+1;
  int my_left=rank-1;

  if (rank==(size-1)) {
    std::cout << "Send/Recv problem" << '\n';
    my_right=0;
  }
  else if(rank==0){
    my_left=size-1;
  }

  MPI_Send(arr,arrsize,MPI_INT,my_right,0,MPI_COMM_WORLD);
  MPI_Recv(arr,arrsize,MPI_INT,my_left,0,MPI_COMM_WORLD,MPI_STATUS_IGNORE);

  //output the looped values
  std::cout <<"from rank " <<rank << '\n';
  for (int i = 0; i < arrsize; i++) {
    std::cout << arr[i] << '\n';
  }

  delete [] arr;


  //scatter and gather

  //fill an array on the first process with size numbers
  int *b=new int[1];

  if (rank==0) {
    std::cout << "Scatter/gather problem" << '\n';
  }
  int *a=new int[size];
  for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    if (rank==0) {
      a[i]=i;
    }
    else{
      a[i]=0;  
    }
  }

  //scatter it to the rest of the processes
  MPI_Scatter(a,1,MPI_INT,b,1,MPI_INT,0,MPI_COMM_WORLD);

  //print output
  std::cout << "on rank "<< rank<< " value= "<<b[0] << '\n';

  //gather it back

  //output it on the first

  //delete mpi communicator
  MPI_Finalize();
  return 0;
}
```

## OpenMP

- Shared memory parallelization: multi threads share the same memory space. A fork and join model

in clude `#include <omp.h>` and compile with `-fopenmp`

Define the parallel region with `#pragma omp`

get he rank and size with `omp_get_thread_num()` and   `omp_get_num_threads()` respectively.

set the number of threads with `export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4` or `omp_set_num_threads(4)`.

For loops can be parallelized automatically with `#pragma omp parallel for`
